title: Reference only registered contracts as interlocking message payloads

facts.note: Validation subject_kind is interlocking; interlocking artifacts are identifiable by file kind/path.

Enforced confirm-blocking at CONFIRM; the harness must report the phase. Applies to every payload contract identity referenced by an interlocking message, whether or not the reference itself changed (registry edits/removals can invalidate unchanged references).

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking message's payload names a contract identity that is not an entry in the contracts registry, even though a contract file matching that name exists on disk.
At CONFIRM, an unchanged interlocking message references a payload contract identity whose registry entry was removed or renamed.
At CONFIRM, a plan in which a planner authored or edited an interlocking message payload contract identity to a value absent from the contracts registry.
doesNotFire: Every payload contract identity referenced by interlocking messages is an entry in the contracts registry.
Planning artifacts with no interlocking messages (e.g. plain wagon or acceptance docs that declare no interlocking payloads).
Before CONFIRM (e.g. while a plan is still being drafted); the check is enforced at CONFIRM.

given: An interlocking artifact has messages that reference payload contract identities.
when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (any referenced identity is checked, changed or not).
then: Every payload contract identity referenced by an interlocking message must resolve to an authored/registered entry in the contracts registry (contracts/_contracts.yaml), not merely to a file that glob-matches.
prefer: Look up the identity in the contracts registry, the single source of truth for identity -> path -> theme -> producers -> consumers, and reference an identity that is a member of it.
If the needed contract is not yet registered, plan its authoring and registration as part of the work before referencing it.
When a registry entry is removed or renamed, update the interlocking messages that reference it.
avoid: Pointing the payload at a contract file that merely exists or glob-matches without a registry entry.
Inventing a contract identity in the interlocking that no registry entry backs.
why: The contracts registry is the single source of truth for identity -> path -> theme -> producers -> consumers; a glob-matching file is not sufficient to count as a registered contract.
evidence: On failure, the report names interlocking_id, message_id, contract, and registry_path.
verifier_detail: Validation family: resolution; template: artifact_reference_resolution; variant: planner_train_interlocking_payload_contract_registered.
Phase CONFIRM, enforcement confirm-blocking; subject_kind interlocking. Check all referenced payload contract identities, not only changed ones.
Resolution is by membership in the authored contracts registry (contracts/_contracts.yaml); a filesystem glob match does NOT count as resolution.
Failure evidence fields: interlocking_id, message_id, contract, registry_path.
audit: Term registered_contract: a payload contract identity must be a member of the authored contracts registry (contracts/_contracts.yaml), the single source of truth for identity -> path -> theme -> producers -> consumers (#1330 / ...).
